content_body: Patient admitted for acute retrosternal chest pain and dyspnea. 12-lead ECG showed sinus tachycardia (115 bpm). Troponin I elevated at 0.45 ng/mL. Discharged on Metoprolol 25mg daily and Aspirin 81mg. Diagnosis: Non-ST Elevation Acute Coronary Syndrome rule-out.
Chest X-Ray (PA and Lateral): Moderate cardiomegaly with mild pulmonary vascular congestion. Lung fields clear of acute focal infiltrates. No pleural effusion.
Cardiac Biomarkers Panel: Troponin I 0.45 ng/mL (High, ref <0.04), CK-MB 6.8 ng/mL (Elevated), BNP 420 pg/mL (High). Flagged cardiac enzyme elevation.
Cardiology outpatient follow-up. Patient reports resolution of resting chest tightness. Resting heart rate controlled at 68 bpm on Metoprolol. Transthoracic echocardiogram scheduled.
Echocardiogram Complete: Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) 52%. Mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. Grade 1 diastolic dysfunction.
Routine cardiology review. Vitals stable at BP 122/78 mmHg, HR 64 bpm. Patient walking 30 minutes daily without angina. Continue current medical therapy.

Scheduled endocrine follow-up for uncontrolled Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus. Patient reports persistent bilateral burning pain in lower extremities. Referred to podiatry for diabetic neuropathy evaluation.
Glycated Hemoglobin & Lipid Panel: HbA1c 9.4% (Critical High, ref <5.7%), Fasting Plasma Glucose 198 mg/dL (High), Total Cholesterol 245 mg/dL, Triglycerides 230 mg/dL.
Podiatry consultation note: Bilateral lower extremity monofilament testing demonstrates reduced protective sensation in L4-S1 distribution. No active foot ulcerations or skin breakdown.
Short stay admission for acute diabetic hyperosmolar management. IV hydration and subcutaneous insulin protocol initiated. Stabilized and discharged on Insulin Glargine 20 units nightly.
Repeat Metabolic Surveillance: Fasting Blood Glucose improved to 132 mg/dL. Urine microalbumin-to-creatinine ratio 45 mg/g (Microalbuminuria detected).
Endocrinology progress note: Blood sugars trending lower (morning fasting 110-130 mg/dL). Gabapentin 300mg QHS initiated for peripheral neuropathy symptoms.
Orthopedic evaluation for severe lower back pain radiating down right posterior leg to lateral foot (L5 dermatome). Straight leg raise test positive on right at 35 degrees.
MRI Lumbar Spine without contrast: L4-L5 broad-based posterior disc herniation with moderate central canal stenosis and right lateral recess nerve root compression.
Outpatient surgical center discharge: Fluoroscopy-guided right L4-L5 transforaminal epidural steroid injection completed without complication. Pain score decreased from 8/10 to 3/10.
Post-injection follow-up: Patient reports 70% relief in radicular leg pain. Physical therapy prescribed twice weekly for lumbar core stabilization.
Lumbar Spine X-Ray (Flexion/Extension): No dynamic lumbar spondylolisthesis or gross spinal instability identified.
Physical therapy completion memo: Core strength improved. Patient walking 2 miles without paresthesias. Discharged to home exercise program.
Inpatient admission for acute COPD exacerbation and productive cough with purulent sputum. Oxygen saturation 88% on room air at presentation. Treated with IV Methylprednisolone and Duoneb.
High-Resolution Chest CT: Severe panlobular emphysematous changes in bilateral upper lobes. No acute pulmonary embolism. Mild bronchial wall thickening.
Arterial Blood Gas (ABG): pH 7.34, PaCO2 52 mmHg (Elevated/Hypercapnia), PaO2 62 mmHg, HCO3 28 mmol/L. Suggestive of compensated respiratory acidosis.
Pulmonology clinic review: Patient completed 5-day prednisone taper. Switched to Trelegy Ellipta once daily. Strongly counseled on smoking cessation.
Pulmonary Function Tests (PFT): FEV1/FVC ratio 58% (Moderate persistent airflow obstruction). Significant post-bronchodilator reversibility (+14% in FEV1).
Routine pulmonary surveillance: Dyspnea on exertion improved to mMRC Grade 1. Oxygen saturation 96% on room air. Flu and Pneumococcal vaccinations administered.
Neurology consultation for intractable hemicranial throbbing headaches occurring 4-5 times per week, accompanied by scintillating scotoma, nausea, and photophobia.
Brain MRI with and without IV Gadolinium: Normal brain parenchyma. No intracranial mass lesion, acute infarct, or vascular malformation. Ventricles normal in caliber.
Neurology follow-up: Diagnosis confirmed as Chronic Migraine with Aura. Initiated preventive therapy with Topiramate 25mg nightly, titrated to 50mg. Prescribed Rizatriptan for abortive use.
Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP): Serum Creatinine 0.8 mg/dL, AST 18 U/L, ALT 22 U/L, Serum Bicarbonate 22 mEq/L. Normal renal and hepatic baseline.
Headache clinic review: Migraine frequency decreased from 18 days/month to 6 days/month on Topiramate. Mild distal paresthesias noted as known side effect.
Long-term neurology follow-up: Headache log shows sustained reduction. Patient tolerating medication well with good quality of life improvement.
Nephrology referral for progressive decline in renal function. History of hypertension for 20 years. Mild bilateral pitting pedal edema noted.
Renal Function Panel: Serum Creatinine 2.1 mg/dL (High, baseline 1.6), Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN) 38 mg/dL (High), eGFR 34 mL/min/1.73m2. Stage 3b Chronic Kidney Disease.
Renal Ultrasound with Doppler: Bilateral kidneys symmetric with increased echogenicity compatible with chronic medical renal disease. No hydronephrosis or renal artery stenosis.
Urinalysis & 24-hr Protein: Proteinuria 850 mg/24hr (Elevated). Serum Potassium 4.9 mmol/L. Urine microscopy negative for red cell casts.
Nephrology management note: Adjusted Lisinopril to Losartan 25mg daily. Placed on renal-protective dietary protocol with sodium <2g/day and moderate protein intake.
Surveillance Renal Panel: Serum Creatinine stable at 2.0 mg/dL, eGFR 36 mL/min. Serum potassium stable at 4.7 mmol/L. Proteinuria decreased to 520 mg/24hr.
Emergency admission for severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back following heavy meal. Serum Lipase markedly elevated. Managed with aggressive NPO and IV crystalloids.
Pancreatic Enzymes & LFT: Serum Lipase 1,250 U/L (Critical High, ref <60), Serum Amylase 410 U/L (High), Total Bilirubin 1.1 mg/dL, ALT 35 U/L.
Abdominal Ultrasound: Gallbladder contains multiple small acoustic shadowing calculi (cholelithiasis). Common bile duct diameter normal at 4mm. No pericholecystic fluid.
Gastroenterology post-discharge review: Acute pancreatitis resolved. Diagnosed with mild gallstone pancreatitis. Elective outpatient laparoscopic cholecystectomy recommended.
Surgical discharge note: Elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy completed without incident. Pathology confirmed chronic cholecystitis with cholelithiasis.
Post-operative surgical check: Incisions healing well. Tolerating regular low-fat diet without nausea or abdominal pain. Normal bowel habits restored.
Rheumatology evaluation for symmetric joint stiffness lasting >2 hours in morning, affecting bilateral MCP, PIP, and wrist joints for 4 months.
Rheumatology Serologies: Rheumatoid Factor (RF) positive at 120 IU/mL, Anti-CCP antibodies >250 U/mL (Strongly positive), ESR 48 mm/hr, CRP 24 mg/L.
Bilateral Hands & Wrists X-Rays: Periarticular osteopenia and mild joint space narrowing in 2nd and 3rd MCP joints bilaterally. No definite marginal erosions.
Rheumatology treatment plan: Established diagnosis of Seropositive Rheumatoid Arthritis. Initiated Methotrexate 15mg weekly with Folic Acid 1mg daily and short-term Prednisone 10mg.
Drug Monitoring Panel: CBC and Liver enzymes normal on Methotrexate (ALT 20 U/L, WBC 6.8). CRP decreased to 8.2 mg/L. ESR improved to 22 mm/hr.
Rheumatology follow-up: Morning stiffness reduced to 20 minutes. Joint tenderness count reduced from 14 to 3 joints. Prednisone tapered successfully to 2.5mg.
Breast health consultation following screening mammogram showing 1.2 cm suspicious architectural distortion with microcalcifications in right upper outer quadrant.
Diagnostic Mammogram & Breast Ultrasound: BI-RADS Category 4C (High suspicion for malignancy). 1.4 cm irregular hypoechoic mass with indistinct margins at 10:00 position.
Outpatient biopsy note: Ultrasound-guided 14-gauge core needle biopsy of right breast mass performed. Titanium marker clip successfully deployed at biopsy site.
Surgical Pathology Report: Invasive Ductal Carcinoma, Grade 1 (Well differentiated). Estrogen Receptor (ER) positive (95%), Progesterone Receptor (PR) positive (80%), HER2-neu negative.
Multidisciplinary tumor board conference review: Clinical Stage I (cT1c N0 M0). Recommended breast-conserving surgery (lumpectomy) with sentinel lymph node biopsy.
Post-operative surgical discharge: Right partial mastectomy and sentinel lymph node dissection completed. Sentinel lymph nodes (2/2) negative for metastatic carcinoma.
Emergency hospital admission: 29-year-old male presenting with acute migratory right lower quadrant abdominal pain, anorexia, and low-grade fever (100.8F). McBurney point tenderness positive.
Abdomen/Pelvis CT with IV Contrast: Distended appendix measuring 11mm in diameter with wall thickening and surrounding peri-appendiceal fat stranding. Consistent with Acute Appendicitis.
Emergency Lab Panel: WBC count 16.4 x10^3/uL (Leukocytosis with left shift, 84% neutrophils). Serum lactate normal at 1.1 mmol/L.
Surgical discharge note: Emergent laparoscopic appendectomy performed. Operative findings confirmed acute suppurative appendicitis without perforation. Tolerating diet on discharge.
Two-week surgical post-op: Incision sites healed with no erythema or drainage. Normal bowel movements. Cleared for full physical activity and return to work.
Routine clinic encounter: Patient fully recovered from appendectomy. Vitals normal. No gastrointestinal complaints.
Inpatient admission for Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP). Presenting with fever (102.2F), right pleuritic chest pain, and productive cough with rust-colored sputum.
Chest Radiograph (PA/Lateral): Dense alveolar consolidation in right middle and lower lobes with visible air bronchograms. No pneumothorax.
Infectious Disease Panel: Sputum Gram Stain shows gram-positive diplococci. Blood cultures positive for Streptococcus pneumoniae (sensitive to Ceftriaxone). Procalcitonin 1.8 ng/mL (Elevated).
Infectious disease follow-up: Completed 7-day course of oral Amoxicillin-Clavulanate. Fever completely resolved, cough significantly improved. Energy levels recovering.
Repeat Chest X-Ray: Substantial clearing of right middle and lower lobe consolidation. Minimal residual linear atelectasis.
Pulmonary wellness visit: Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally. No dyspnea on exertion. Pneumococcal conjugate vaccination administered.
Emergency department admission for acute left calf pain, swelling, and localized erythema following 14-hour international flight. Left calf circumference 3cm larger than right.
Venous Duplex Ultrasound (Left Lower Extremity): Non-compressible left popliteal and posterior tibial veins with intraluminal thrombus. Confirms Acute Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT).
Coagulation & D-Dimer: D-Dimer markedly elevated at 2,850 ng/mL (ref <500). PT 12.1 sec, INR 1.0, aPTT 28 sec. Baseline renal function normal.
Hematology/Vascular clinic: Started on Apixaban (Eliquis) 10mg BID for 7 days, transitioning to 5mg BID for 3 months. Counseled on signs of bleeding and pulmonary embolism.
Follow-up Venous Ultrasound: Significant recanalization of left popliteal vein with resolving residual thrombus. Good spontaneous flow.
Vascular progress note: Left leg swelling completely resolved. Patient walking daily without calf tenderness. Plan to complete 3-month course of Apixaban.
Psychiatric intake evaluation: Patient presents with 6-month history of persistent depressed mood, anhedonia, early morning awakening, and severe generalized anxiety with panic episodes.
Diagnostic Psychiatric Workup: TSH 2.1 mIU/L (Normal), Free T4 1.2 ng/dL, Serum Vitamin B12 480 pg/mL, Vitamin D 25-OH 18 ng/mL (Low/Insufficiency).

Psychiatry treatment session: Diagnosis of Major Depressive Disorder (Moderate) and Generalized Anxiety Disorder. Initiated Sertraline 25mg daily, titrating to 50mg. Ergocalciferol 50,000 IU weekly for Vitamin D deficiency.
Medication management follow-up: PHQ-9 depression score improved from 18 to 11. GAD-7 anxiety score decreased from 16 to 8. Sertraline dose increased to 75mg daily. No suicidal ideation.
Psychotherapy progress note: Patient reports improved sleep architecture (sleeping 7 hours nightly). Engaging actively in cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) exercises.
Repeat Nutritional Surveillance: Vitamin D 25-OH normalized to 44 ng/mL. Patient reports improved overall stamina and daily mood stability.
Dermatology total body skin exam: Asymmetric, irregularly pigmented 7mm macule with dark brown and black variegation identified on right upper back. High clinical suspicion for dysplastic lesion.
Minor surgical procedure: Complete saucerization excisional biopsy of 7mm pigmented lesion on right upper back with 2mm clinical margins performed under local anesthesia.
Dermatopathology Report: Compound Melanocytic Nevus with Severe Architectural and Cytological Atypia (Severely Dysplastic Nevus). Peripheral and deep surgical margins free of lesion.
Dermatology follow-up: Discussed pathology results. Due to severe atypia, recommended conservative 5mm re-excision to ensure complete histological clearance.
Outpatient wide local excision: Re-excision of prior biopsy site on right upper back with 5mm margins. Closed with layered sutures.
Suture removal and final review: Re-excision pathology confirmed completely negative scar tissue. Scheduled for routine 6-month surveillance skin exam.
Emergency presentation for acute severe right flank pain radiating to groin, accompanied by microscopic hematuria and severe nausea. Given IV Ketorolac and Ondansetron.
Non-Contrast Helical CT Abdomen/Pelvis: 5.5mm obstructing calculus at right ureterovesical junction (UVJ) causing mild right hydroureteronephrosis. Left kidney normal.
Urinalysis & Renal Panel: Urine RBC >50/HPF (Gross microscopic hematuria), Urine WBC 2-4/HPF, Nitrite negative. Serum Creatinine normal at 1.0 mg/dL.
Urology outpatient check: Patient successfully passed stone at home after 5 days on Tamsulosin (Flomax) 0.4mg. Flank pain completely resolved. Stone submitted for analysis.
Stone Mineral Composition Analysis: 100% Calcium Oxalate Monohydrate. 24-hour urine metabolic evaluation ordered.
Metabolic Stone Prevention review: 24-hour urine showed mild hypercalciuria with low urinary volume (1.2L). Instructed on aggressive fluid hydration (>2.5L/day) and low-sodium diet.
